notes.title: Survival Tips For Your Next Crew Experience
notes.content:
Hello! It’s Jon from Runner Duck here. Badlands Crew is out next week, 28th April! Thank you for all your support so far. It’s been a big project for us, and we’re really excited that you’ll all finally be able to play it!

As it’s now close to the game’s release, I thought we should write a different kind of news post, and give you a few little tips and tricks which will help you out along your way in the Badlands.

[h3][b]USE THE MIDDLE-CLICK SHORTCUT MENU[/b][/h3]
One of the new features in Badlands Crew is the middle-click shortcut menu. With a crew member selected, middle click somewhere on the screen. The shortcut popup menu will appear. It has shortcuts for common actions, such as sending crew to other stations, attacking enemy boarders, or repairing broken systems. This is a great way to quickly do common actions (e.g. sending a crew member to a rejuvenator to heal, or quickly sending someone to repair the engine). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/187ca3739a5af2a967b5d5d817318bd8629f8795.jpg[/img][i]The middle-click shortcut menu[/i]

This works especially well for Badlands Crew, as unlike our previous games, your vehicle may have multiple rejuvenators, and loads of turrets. Don’t forget to try it out, and hopefully it’ll bring your command of your crew to a new level!

[h3][b]RE-BIND YOUR KEYS IF YOU DON'T GET ALONG WITH THE DEFAULTS[/b][/h3]
We’ve had a lot of back and forth on what the default keyboard controls should be. We’ve set them to what we think will be the most consistent throughout the title, and give you the best chance of survival long-term. However, some players will probably prefer to remap their vehicle nudge/speed adjustment inputs to WASD. This is fine! Please do this if you find it easier or more natural.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/49a16032c7c69c9f46ce2a657d8b4750927987cf.jpg[/img][i]The control rebinding options[/i]

Control rebinding options can be found in the options menu. There are also options for axis inversion.

[h3][b]USE 'SLOW TIME' WHENEVER YOU'RE UNDER PRESSURE[/b][/h3]
Things can get intense quickly in the Badlands. If things aren’t going so well, you can use ‘Slow Time’ to give yourself a bit of time to get all your problems sorted. By default ‘Slow Time’ is bound to the Shift key.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/895d04f9ecafb6fc0eaa57bb3caefa7d7a084270.jpg[/img][i]The ‘Slow Time’ shortcut (Top-Left Corner of the UI)[/i]

Don’t forget to use ‘Slow Time’ - it really can give you the time you need to save your crew and your Battle Wagon.

[h3][b]UPGRADE YOUR VEHICLE'S FUEL CAPACITY EARLY[/b][/h3]
There’s nothing worse than running out of fuel in the middle of the Badlands. I would recommend adding an ‘auxiliary fuel tank’ to your vehicle as soon as you unlock it. As the game progresses, and you are able to, I’d recommend adding a couple more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/e65bb948a3bb723478604b66dc85e814fd33d3bc.jpg[/img][i]An auxiliary fuel tank being added to a vehicle in the garage[/i]

[h3][b]DON'Y GET EATEN BY A SANDWORM[/b][/h3]
Don’t get eaten by a sandworm. If your vehicle sits idle for too long, there’s a chance a sandworm will snap it up. Repair your engine, get someone in the driving seat, and get moving!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/36f546282f3e5b962e1f3a197c328f8a654323ec.jpg[/img][i]A sandworm about to eat a Battle Wagon[/i]

If you start seeing a sandworm rising up from the ground around you… stay calm, and try to escape through the gaps!

[h3][b]USE ABILITIES (USE THEM ALOT)[/b][/h3]
If you’re not using your crew’s Abilities, you’re not getting the most out of them! It can be easy to forget you have them in the heat of battle, so use ‘Slow Time’ too if you need to! Using your crew’s Abilities strategically can make the difference between success and failure!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/40874abbc1220e400bb523c9fac3ce87e4f740bc.jpg[/img][i]The ‘Swerve’ ability being used[/i]

If things are intense, get your driver to use ‘Swerve’ - enemies will have a harder time aiming at you, and this can buy you some time…

[h3][b]LOOK OUT FOR OPTIONAL OBJECTIVES[/b][/h3]
There’s loads to discover in the Badlands. Crew at your Command Station can be used to spot Optional Objectives. Of course, be careful not to get in over your head - if you’re low on fuel, or your crew are in poor health, then perhaps it’s best to stay on mission!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/1f3de7339084036ff6c0203b095b11965c36d5d9.jpg[/img][i]A cache bunker containing some blueprints[/i]

Finding relics around the Badlands will reward you with additional Blueprints, giving you more options for your Battle Wagon and your crew’s gear.

[h3][b]USE ESCAPE DEVICES TO SAVE YOUR CREW[/b][/h3]
If it looks like you’re not going to get back to base in one piece, but you want to save some of your crew: use an Escape Device. It’s not always worth battling on - escape, and live to fight another day! Unlike Bomber Crew, crewmates who use an Escape Device will always survive (however, they may not always return to base instantly, and might need to be rescued in a subsequent mission).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/63423b9411f12df3e92f6fa75e5ab2f1d5119811.jpg[/img][i]An escape device on a Battle Wagon[/i]

[h3][b]UPGRADE YOUR CREW & GARAGE FACILITIES[/b][/h3]
Upgrading your Crew & Garage facilities will lessen the blow of losing your crew or vehicle, so it’s definitely a good idea to remember to do this.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/4c506e331abc73c4683a7b6f894d7c989a78a257.jpg[/img][i]Upgrading Crew Facilities [/i]

You can upgrade your Crew facilities to increase the starting level of new recruits.
You can also upgrade your Garage facilities so that more of your Battle Wagon is salvaged (for free) when it is lost.

[h3][b]THERE'S MORE TO LEARN![/b][/h3]
There’s even more to learn than I’ve written here… but hopefully these tips will help you get off to a good start! The Badlands is a dangerous place. You will lose crewmates, you will fail missions… but I hope that ultimately you will triumph. We’re all looking forward to the game’s launch on Monday. See you then!

[h3][b]TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THE BUNDLES![/b][/h3]
Our last tip applies IRL! If you own Bomber Crew and/or Space Crew, you'll get an extra discount when Badlands Crew launches, so make sure to take advantage of stacking launch and bundle discounts!

– Jon, Dave, Joe, Greg (Runner Duck)

notes.title: Development Update – Enemy Faction Spotlight: The Gun Nutz
notes.content:
Hello, Dave from Runner Duck here! I wanted to complete our series of posts about the enemy factions you’ll face in Badlands Crew with a look at ‘The Gun Nutz’…

To the South East of the starting area of Home Plateau lies the red eroded desert of the Lower Badlands, where you’ll run into The Gun Nutz patrolling its valleys and canyons.

The Gun Nutz are descendants of a community of preppers who sprung into action as society crumbled,
gleefully raiding army equipment storage sites, claiming the vast majority of conventional firearms and military vehicles in the land.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/6b96d8183a6651ed46f5157e6b82c88a0e5bafff.jpg[/img][i]A heavily armed Gun Nutz patrol harassing an ambushed Battle Wagon[/i]

Their commander in chief is the ruthless disciplinarian, Major Krank; as brutal to his own subordinates as he is to his enemies. Rumours abound that during his raids on military storage sites, he stumbled upon the last viable nuclear warhead in existence, which he wields to cow any potential challengers into submission.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/c22ac2c608fa2bd63d6c38e7d8fd55bcedbb1717.jpg[/img][i]Early Concept Art for the Gun Nutz Faction’s Warlord (Major Krank), Symbol and crew characters[/i]

As for vehicles, The Gun Nutz bring to bear a range of military rides including jeeps, hummers, MRAPs, pickups and half tracks. With their ready-made fleet of piercing and blast damage resistant war machines, it’s wise to prepare carefully before confronting their patrols! Perhaps try ‘turning up the heat’ on them ;).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/8b0f176f2e343c9fcaa6a97d19b5a15cb49d0f56.jpg[/img][i]The Gun Nutz’ fleet of military vehicles in our ‘Virtual Parking Lot’.[/i]

The Gun Nutz’ armoury comprises a range of lethal conventional weapons, including machine guns, rifles, shotguns and grenade launchers. They have guns that are effective from close to long range, so keep those heads on a swivel!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/44ac4a228078bd88558e940ace5f9b81ba3c410b.png[/img][i]L-R: A good ol’ 50 cal, a water-cooled electric drive ‘Scattermaster’ auto shotgun, ‘Doomster’ sawn off shotgun[/i]

Time for me to get back to the finishing touches on the project; it's been a long road, but now we’re just one week from release!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2078230/Badlands_Crew/

Thanks for reading!
Dave

notes.title: Sneak Peak - Badlands Enemy Faction Spotlight: The Klowns
notes.content:
Hi! Jon from Runner Duck here, sharing a quick look at another of the enemy factions in Badlands Crew - ‘The Klowns’.

To the East of the Lower Badlands, in the glistening whiteness of the Dessicated Salt Flats, is where you’re most likely to first encounter the Klowns faction. Devoid of shame, the Klowns intentionally appear ridiculous in order to obfuscate their true ruthless nature.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/6630fa11769c9cc1b170e2c7428592ba77067748.jpg[/img]
[i]A Klowns “Ice Screamer” and “Re-Educator” terrorising the Salt Flats[/i]

The Klowns are ruled by “Giggles the Klown”, their psychopathic leader in greasepaint and a clown wig. Many of his followers who initially fell for his charming, harmless facade wish to escape from his faction, but the consequences for those captured are severe. They also hold territory around the edges of The Atomic City, and further to the East in Krazed Quarry.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/b09d0232b531375c68b3485da5ec1ee7aee8f597.jpg[/img]
[i]Early Concept Art for the Klown Faction’s Warlord, Symbol and crew characters[/i]

The Klown’s fleet of vehicles feature some unusual choices, matching their origins as a chaotic circus troupe; their brightly coloured food trucks, school buses and even dodgems may look comical, but are bristling with weapons and pack a punch!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/9a9769980353dc7315b68a79b3b298f019dfa1da.jpg[/img]
[i]Klown vehicles in our ‘Virtual Parking Lot’ scene, where we assemble the many variations[/i]

The Klowns primarily use two types of weaponry: toxic gas weapons which can inflict poison damage, and makeshift pneumatic cannons, firing golf balls or even bowling balls, which deal blunt damage and can cause crew to become stunned. Having spent too much time fooling around with their own toxic weapon supplies they are somewhat immune to toxic damage, so you’re better off using other weapon types against them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/7ee917205dd728fcf31f1e6339fa1c6c41642d9c.png[/img]
[i]L-R: ‘The Stinger’ BB gun, ‘Toxic Balloon Launcher’, ‘Screaming Splitter’ Bowling Ball Cannon[/i]

I hope you have the last laugh when you go up against Giggles in the Badlands! Remember to wishlist Badlands Crew ahead of launch on the 28th!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2078230/Badlands_Crew/

That’s all for now, we’ve got to finish the game, because it’s out soon!
Jon

notes.title: This strategic space sim is a free Steam game, but not for long
notes.content:
From Starfield to No Man's Sky and beyond, if you're in the mood for an interstellar adventure, there's no shortage of ways to do so. But while the grandiose machinations of Elite Dangerous and Star Citizen can be bold, the best space games are often those smaller-scale strategy games and roguelikes such as FTL and the upcoming Breachway. If that sounds up your alley, then Space Crew might be just what you're after - we labeled it a "compact, confident, bite-sized roguelite" in our review, and now it's yours as a free Steam game if you're quick.

notes.content:
Big news Crewmates! 

From the makers of Bomber Crew and Space Crew, comes a brand-new, high-octane adventure: 
[h2][b]Badlands Crew![/b][/h2]
With a host of innovative new features such as vehicle building and customization, a dynamic and evolving campaign, and tactically diverse and intense combat encounters, Badlands Crew will be the biggest and the best game in the Crew series. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2078230/Badlands_Crew/
[previewyoutube=DMhca33A6Ek;full][/previewyoutube]
Create, customize and command your battle wagon to conquer crazed enemy factions and save innocent survivors scattered throughout the lawless Badlands in the aftermath of a devastating apocalypse. With deep and dynamic vehicle customization, build your own beast of a battle wagon ready to head out into the carnage and succeed in your voyage. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33019968/f84c1a27baee0618905f84a86afdea4bee91d747.gif[/img]

Transform your rag-tag crew of skill-less grunts into a legendary unit of elite road warriors – with an array of skills, abilities and perks to choose from to suit your unique playstyle.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33019968/e430979d41041c559542798feecaa73936470503.gif[/img]

Combat requires commanders to multitask under immense pressure. Think quickly on your feet and manage your crew individually in the heat of battle to man guns, repair vehicle components, heal injured crewmates and repel boarders. Drive and navigate to avoid environmental hazards such as sandstorms, volcanic eruptions and giant sandworms whilst fighting off waves of enemy combatants. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33019968/f0fd917fd430b49cafdf5ec654a8139e7cb1ab65.gif[/img]

The Badlands is a vast desert landscape, filled with strongholds and outposts to overcome on your journey. Your decisions change the campaign map as faction influence declines and grows based on the outcome of your battles. Smart decision-making within the safety of The Citadel when planning routes, customizing vehicles and training your crew is just as important as critical calls made during the heat of battle. 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33019968/04a1c4da79d9aa5daec03e38fe8417a689eadd11.gif[/img]

And most of all, go head-to-head with the wild enemy factions that roam the Badlands. The Gun Nutz, Pyros, Vultures and Klowns are each led by a crazed warlord boss. Going head-to-head to defeat them in combat will require skill and planning as each faction has their own unique weaponry and combat tactics. You will need to adapt your strategies, your battle wagon build and your crew’s skills to succeed! 

Well, what are you waiting for? Wishlist now and get ready for your first mission into the treacherous Badlands!

notes.title: Just like Space Crew, WDC is on a mission! 🐳
notes.content:
We are thrilled to be able to support WDC in this year's Jingle Jam!

[quote][url=https://uk.whales.org/]WDC [/url]has been incredibly lucky to be a [url=https://www.jinglejam.co.uk/]Jingle Jam[/url] featured charity since 2016 raising over £1.6 million for our vital work to protect whales and dolphins across the globe from the many threats they face. 

The incredible support from the generous and passionate Jingle Jam community has had a huge impact on several key areas of our work.  

Jingle Jam 2021 helped to fund our innovative project to reduce entanglements of whales here in the UK, and urgent work within the [url=https://uk.whales.org/our-4-goals/stop-whaling/stop-dolphin-hunts/small-whale-and-dolphin-hunts-in-the-faroe-islands/]Faroes to end the cruel dolphin hunts[/url]. 

This year we are so excited to share that we are planning to use the funds raised from Jingle Jam 2022 to support our work in Scotland, with three vital projects: 

[h3]Shorewatch Expansion[/h3]  
Shorewatch is WDC’s citizen science programme aimed at inspiring love and understanding for whales and dolphins by collating sightings of whales, dolphins and porpoises from the Scottish coast. We will support more young adults (18+) to participate in the Shorewatch programme and engage with nature, inspiring them to learn about the ocean and champion better protection for whales, dolphins and the planet. 
[previewyoutube=KxB2I19zj4E;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Scottish Dolphin Centre educational exhibition upgrade  [/h3]
Enhance our exhibitions with interactive displays and experiences to provide more exciting educational opportunities for visitors as well as encouraging support for our ongoing campaigns. We will also make the exhibition more accessible, thus allowing a wider diversity of children and people of all ages to enjoy and learn about whales and dolphins, and how to better protect the ocean and the planet. 
[previewyoutube=avYJhLbLd7Y;full][/previewyoutube]


[h3]Tackling chemical pollution in Scottish waters  [/h3]
Chemical pollution is devastating the ocean and its inhabitants and has put an entire population of orcas living in Scottish waters at risk of extinction. WDC will undertake research and develop a campaign to drive positive changes to chemical legislation to protect whales and dolphins and stop species from becoming extinct. 
[previewyoutube=uj_NySIEXms;full][/previewyoutube] 

  

Find out more here:  

WDC: [url=https://uk.whales.org/]https://uk.whales.org/[/url] 

Jingle Jam 2022: [url=https://www.jinglejam.co.uk/]https://www.jinglejam.co.uk/[/url] [/quote]

Space simulation game Space Crew is a tongue-in-cheek Star Trek-style romp that mixes elements of FTL and other roguelites in a fun and friendly manner. In our review, we lamented the lack of management elements and meaningful choices, but we appreciated it for what it was.

The new edition introduces a host of new content such as a new campaign, a new mechanic in the form of away missions, and even new 'legendary' crew members.

The campaign will see you take on a droid army led by a rogue group of androids, while the new crew members will feature superior stats and abilities compared to the regular crew. Finally, the new away missions can feature a range of challenges, from exploration and puzzles, to good old-fashioned gunfights. This expansion is not only the largest content drop for Space Crew to date, it's 100% free for existing owners of the base game.

notes.title: Space Crew Update 1.2 is Out Now!
notes.content:
Hi Everyone,

We’re happy to announce that the latest update to Space Crew is now available!

This time, we’ve focused on a few areas that have been highlighted in the great feedback we’ve received from the community.

Firstly, we’ve added a range of new [b]Events and Encounters[/b] to punctuate missions with more variety and surprises. In addition to this, the [b]Comms Station[/b] has received upgrades in the form of a new [b]Hacking Function[/b] and [b]Mission Map[/b].

You’ll have more control during combat in the form of the new [b]Custom Waypoint[/b] and [b]Prioritise Target[/b] functions accessible when in [b]Tagging Mode[/b].

Lastly, we’ve added [b]MK3 Weapon pods[/b] to complete that ultimate loadout.

There are also a few minor improvements and additions, which we’ve listed below.

Once more, thanks for all your feedback and suggestions, they’ve been enormously helpful to us as we work to enhance the game.

We hope you jump back in and enjoy these new features and content, and please do continue to let us know what you think!

[i]Dave, Jon, Joe & Greg (Our new team member!)
Runner Duck[/i]

[h1]Release Notes:[/h1]

[h2]New Events and Encounters[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/2e659c65b00e2df8b81d2fb3b42559fa69fb3933.jpg[/img]
You’ll encounter cosmic phenomena such as [b]Ion Storms[/b] that may cause intermittent power outages (We’ve added the ability to quickly repair the effects of EMP on the ship’s reactor, so this can be combatted).

You’ll be confronted with [b]Meteor Showers[/b] that bombard your shields and hull, and [b]Neutrino Flares[/b] that can damage systems and spark onboard fires. You may also encounter a [b]Passing Radioactive Comet[/b], which will bombard your crew with radiation, calling for a hasty escape from the sector.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/6d752c447293c40dd22df9bfc3b507c96b82179e.jpg[/img]
Strange Phasmid Artifacts may be encountered, such as the [b]Phasmid Beacon[/b], which will summon Phasmid forces if not hacked in time. Another hackable artefact is the [b]Phasmid Comms Relay[/b], which will broadcast a self-destruct signal to all enemy ships in the sector if you can keep your cool and successfully hack it while under attack.

Every so often, you may find a discarded [b]Phasmid Wormhole Drive[/b] floating in space. Once hacked, these can provide a useful shortcut through the mission. Be careful, as these drives are unstable, and you may end up stuck in the wormhole for a duration, along with some very annoyed Phasmids!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/dca866b88d36fe8a4ed93eee021793ffd6269d26.jpg[/img]
The Phasmids have been busy establishing more outposts around the Galaxies; take out their shield generators and hit their reactors hard to obliterate them.

And be wary of the new [b]Phasmid Frigates[/b], which have been tasked with scanning sectors for UDF craft, ready to jump in and attack!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/c31468b21cd7fd67afff9fba5b49c2d5bb080c84.jpg[/img]
[b]UDF Aid Stations[/b] will provide much-needed respite - simply land at them to replenish your crew’s health and recharge your med bay. But be on your guard, some of these outposts have been overrun by Phasmid troops!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/a86a2e2069434589704ff274a8e262a9911316a6.jpg[/img]
As the war for the fate of Earth rages on, you’ll encounter [b]Ongoing Space Battles[/b] that require your assistance, and plenty of debris left in their aftermath.

[h2]Custom Waypoints[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/7e776ce8885a7b54cae46da1acedd56f644f46c0.jpg[/img]
You now have more control over the heading of your ship, thanks to the Custom Waypoint feature. Just enter Tagging Mode and follow the prompt to point your ship in the desired direction. This is extra useful for ensuring your gunners have the best angle on their targets.

[h2]Prioritise Targets[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/d0d0daa5900268249271d28e50f0cd9742f8d81a.jpg[/img]
Another new feature accessible in Tagging Mode allows you to specify a tagged fighter as the priority target. Use this to take out key threats such as Phasmid Docking Craft and Drone Carriers.

[h2]‘Return Crew to Stations’ shortcut Panel[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/6be1d7e97a91fb271302a8773196eba70177e0f8.jpg[/img]
A handy set of shortcuts that allow you to quickly get your crew organised in a crisis.
There are options to [b]Return Idle[/b] crew who are not engaged in an action to the nearest appropriate station, [b]Return All[/b] crew to the nearest appropriate station even if they’re busy, and the option to [b]Save Stations[/b] for all crew and then [b]Return to Saved[/b] to get everyone back into their saved seats.

[h2]Comms Station Hacking Function[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/44035f5b4ec36c19b90c47f0323805e84fc1b5fa.jpg[/img]
Larger enemies and some artefacts can now be hacked! Simply tag the hacking marker to get in range, then initiate hacking via the Comms Station. You’ll need to tap out the correct sequence of symbols to successfully complete the hack. The required code may be received from the target during the hack, or in some instances be found marked on the target object. Codes can also be found and stored by scanning [b]Phasmid Code Banks[/b] which may be found floating around in space - these will make hacking a breeze.

[h2]Comms Station Mission Map[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/2f10c1cfa02daa9ad192520167bcb9a10f1cb6bb.jpg[/img]
[i]‘Are we there yet?’[/i]
You can now open a map of the available sectors during a mission. While the map is open, the action is paused to give you some time to get your bearings.

[h2]Mark 3 Weapon Pods[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/87830c0bff0cebf5379df52d63101571e41b63a3.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Space Crew Tips & Tricks
notes.content:
[b]Thank you all for your support of Space Crew so far! We really appreciate all your feedback, and it's great to see so many of you playing already.[/b]

It's dangerous out there in space, so we'd like to share some tips & tricks you can use to make your ride a little (or a lot) more comfortable.

Even in the Runner Duck team, we all use very different approaches when playing through the game, so please feel free to [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1176710/discussions/0/4901564650245179337/]share your own in our forums[/url][/b], We'd be really interested to know what's worked for everyone playing the game so far!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38038049/5e317e90a432394f1fcde3bf4a3004feba29681e.gif[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]Use your abilities[/b]
Crew abilities are essential. If your ship is taking a hammering, use 'Evasive Piloting'. You can also use this to prevent a docking ship from being able to line up, to buy you some time. Got a few fires or repairs to do, but there's a lot going on? Try using 'Stealth Mode' to give yourself some time. Use your engineer's "boost" the reactor and put more energy in to your shields or weapons!

[*] [b]Prioritise repairs[/b]
Repair your engines (don't forget a space suit!), oxygen generator and reactor as soon as you can!

[*] [b]Be prepared for boarders[/b]
Maybe you've seen the ship coming in the distance? Maybe you've heard its docking sound? Get someone ready in advance, and you'll be rid of those Phasmid boarders before they can even start to cause any chaos.

[*][b]Equip your ship with some thought[/b]
Make sure you've got enough med kits! Be sure phase rifles and extinguishers are placed near where you'll need them.

[*] [b]Get your Security Officer on the guns[/b]
Either the front gun, allowing quick access to the security station (for shield replenishing or going in to stealth mode), or the middle gun with a phase rifle nearby for taking out Phasmids.

[*] [b]A fourth gunner[/b]
Want someone else on the guns, too? Your engineer or comms officer are both strong candidates for this. If you're mostly using non-energy weapons, your Engineer can work well. If you're using energy weapons, you may want to have your Engineer using their "boost" skill to allow you to put more power in to your weapons. Or, you can move your Comms Officer to the front gun, allowing them to quickly hop back to their own station for route planning.

[*] [b]Don't worry if you fail[/b]
Replacement crew & ships improve as you go through the game, so you'll never be left with total rubbish - but it may be wise to take on a few low risk missions if you lose everyone.

[*] [b]Escape pods[/b]
Put them on your ship and use them. If everything's gone wrong, there's a good chance of recovery (plus getting the XP gathered so far in the mission). This may also open up rescue missions for crew that don't return immediately.

[*] [b]Take the safest route[/b]
If you're not confident yet, take the safest route.

[*][b]Take the fastest route... at your own risk [/b]
OK, you've got a decent crew, a decent ship... you know your abilities and skills like the back of your hand. Maybe your crew could do with a bit more combat experience? Go fast!

[*] [b]Go home[/b]
Don't be afraid to "Abort" the mission (abort button is on the Captain's station). Med bay gauge empty? Out of med packs? Don't think you'll survive another battle? Try to go home - you'll get the XP you got so far, and keep your ship and crew.

[*] [b]Alien artifacts & cargo pods[/b]
You can scan or retrieve these for some extra spending resources... but, be careful - perhaps the Phasmids are tracking them...?

[*] [b]Repairing engines[/b]
Remember a space suit. Oh, and don't use evasive piloting while your crew member is trying to balance on the engines (If you do, though, you can always tractor beam them back in!).
[/list]
And don't forget: our brand new trailer has five things to help you void complete crew annihilation!

notes.title: Space Crew review - boldly going where plenty have gone before
notes.content:
As a bite-sized roguelite, Space Crew is as compact and well tuned as a new captain's console stuffed with top-of-the-line navigation instruments. After a short few drilling exercises, even rookie cadets will know the difference between their plasma cannons and their shield generators, medical bays and escape pods. Salty space admirals looking to test their strategic mettle, however, might find Space Crew's charming-but-limited gameplay loop a few crates short of a cargo hold.

I named my first ship The Big Dick Enterprise. Juvenile? Probably, but never let it be said that I shy away from the Freudian implications of hurtling through space in a giant metal oblong. Space Crew's cosmos is populated by an aggressive, Grey-like alien species called phasmids. They would eventually destroy the BDE, but I took some satisfaction knowing that their first encounter with Terran diplomacy was getting shot at by a cruiser with a dick joke embossed on the side in bold lettering.

The phasmids are your main source of grief in Space Crew. You'll kick off a mission to deliver cargo, or rescue a stranded astronaut from a doomed station, and eventually be rudely interrupted by some phasmids trying to blast your ship into tiny particles.

notes.title: Space Crew review
notes.content:
Space Crew review
Space Crew’s bouts of tactical damage control are a masterclass in controlled chaos. They’re hampered by a lack of choice in the management segments between them, but not enough to put too big a dent in the fun.

  • Developer: Runner Duck
  • Publisher: Curve Digital
  • Release: October 15th, 2020
  • On: Windows
  • From: Steam
  • Price: £TBC/€TBC/$TBC

When three-man studio Runner Duck released management-tactics game Bomber Crew in 2017, it was rightly praised for turning the “move people around the parts of a large vehicle in an ever-increasing state of panic” aspect of roguelite classic FTL into a whole game. Followup Space Crew takes the action back into space. And while there’s a superficial level of similarity to FTL, with reactor power bars to be allocated, fires to be extinguished with atmosphere vents and all the rest, it’s a different beast.

Crucially, it’s built around the time-honoured structure of bracketing missions with time in a central hub, where you use space coins to upgrade your ship, its crew, their gear and their skills. That back and forth between frantic space missions and dopamine-soaked downtime at HQ is what makes Space Crew so compelling – but it’s also the source of some major, if fixable, limitations.
